records.issue_text: Just-created ruler-only rules are no longer rendered at all during ruler-to-prom propagation, so a newly created rule vanishes from the list until propagation completes
records.rationale: Verified: GrafanaGroupLoader no longer queries the Ruler API nor renders ruler-only rules. The old code rendered `rulerResponse?.rules.map(...)` and, when `promRule` was missing, still returned a `GrafanaRuleListItem` with `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}`. That entire path is removed. The new code renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map((promRule) => ...)` and only checks `isPromResponseLoading`, so if a newly created rule exists only in Ruler during propagation (not yet in the Prometheus groups response), it will not be rendered at all until it appears in `promResponse`.

records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader no longer surfaces query errors from useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery, showing a misleading 'did not find any rule groups' alert when the request actually failed
records.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the component now calls `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery(...)` but only destructures `{ data: promResponse, isLoading: isPromResponseLoading }` and never checks an `error` field. After loading, it does `if (!promResponse) { return <Alert ...> }` (the “did not find any rule groups” case). On an actual request failure, RTK Query typically yields `data`/`promResponse` as `undefined` while setting `error`, so this path would show the misleading “no rule groups” alert instead of an error state. The previous implementation handled error cases (in the deleted loader) explicitly;
